description:
Polyglot Data Modeling for SQL and NoSQL databases, APIs, and storage formats

Hackolade Studio is an intuitive yet powerful application to perform the visually data modeling and schema design of many SQL and NoSQL databases, APIS, and storage formats.
Hackolade Studio combines the graphical representation of collections in an Entity Relationship Diagram, with the graphical representation of the JSON Schema definition of each collection in a hierarchical schema view. Together, these graphical representations provide the schema model for data-at-rest and data-in-motion, plus the documentation of that model. The application is specifically designed around the powerful nature of JSON nested sub-objects and denormalization.
The software facilitates the work of, and the dialog between analysts, architects, designers, developers, testers, DBAs, and operators of systems that are based on such technologies. It also can generate schema scripts and documentation in a variety of machine-readable formats (DDLs, JSON Schema, Avro, Parquet, Protobuf, ...) as well as database instances, or human-readable formats such as HTML, Markdown, and PDF reports.
Instead of having to find data structures tacitly described in the application code, the creation of a database model helps to evaluate design options beforehand, think through the implications of different alternatives, and recognize potential hurdles before committing sizable amounts of development effort. A database model helps plan ahead, in order to minimize later rework. In the end, the modeling process accelerates development, increases quality of the application, and reduces execution risks.
- Ultimate Edition: AI-Assisted Data Modeling with interactive AI chat panel, more info at https://hackolade.com/help/AI-assisteddatamodeling.html
- xDBML: forward- and reverse-engineering of eXtended Database Markup Language, an open markup language for human and AI models to describe the shape of structured data across heterogeneous storage technologies, more info at https://xdbml.org/
- Tech refresh: ElectronJS v45.3.1 (Chromium v156.0.8078.96, NodeJS v24.22.2, V8 v15.6.75.50), and related modules
- Polyglot: added possibility to save a model converted to Polyglot to a remote repository, also in the browser
- PowerDesigner: improved matching of the DBMS of PDM files with Hackolade targets during reverse-engineering
- MEGA: enhanced reverse-engineering of relationship cardinalities
- MEGA: ensured attributes and columns keep the order of the MEGA source during reverse-engineering
- MEGA: ensured only objects on the diagram are reverse-engineered
- MEGA: added reverse-engineering of indexes for Db2 for z/OS
- MEGA: added handling for Mandatory attributes during reverse-engineering
- MEGA: added handling for InitialValue MEGA property to Default during reverse-engineering
- BigQuery, Snowflake: updated minimatch library
- BigQuery, Db2, PostgreSQL, YugabyteDB-YSQL: ensured no redundant SET DEFAULT is generated for a false, 0 or empty default value when the column has a comment
- Cassandra, ScyllaDB: updated fast-xml-parser, node-forge and minimatch libraries
- Db2 for z/OS: added reverse-engineering of indexes from MEGA HOPEX
- DocumentDB, EventBridge, Glue Data Catalog, Neptune, Redshift: updated fast-xml-parser and minimatch libraries
- MongoDB: enhanced the shard key script to use the fields of the selected index, including compound and hashed keys, with unique written as a boolean
- Snowflake: added support for tags defined in another schema or database
